title: Book One · Chapter 68: The Pocket on the Wrong Side
story:
Mum looks at the dress. Then she looks at the paper beside it.

Ronan knows that look. Something is wrong.

The dress belongs to the woman by the table. She touches the new pocket.

“I asked for this side,” she says. She puts her other hand against the dress.

Mum turns over her note. The little drawing has a mark on the left.

“I looked at the front of the dress,” Mum says. “The pocket was on my left. You want it on your own left. That is different from my left.”

“Yes.”

Ronan looks at the pocket. It is a very good pocket. The top is straight. The thread is hard to see.

“Can she use that one too?” he asks.

The woman does not answer at once.

Mum holds up one hand. “That is for her to decide.”

Ronan moves away from the table.

“I do not want two,” the woman says. “I carry a bag on this side. I need the other hand free.”

“Then I will move it,” Mum says. “I am sorry. I cannot finish it before tomorrow morning.”

The woman wants the dress tonight. For a while they talk about a collection time. In the end she agrees to take it tomorrow, early.

The woman leaves. Mum sits down. She does not sew. She rubs her nose.

“You can say, ‘Two pockets are better,’” Ronan says.

“For you, perhaps.”

“She was cross.”

“Yes. I made work for both of us.”

Mum uses a small tool to lift the thread. Ronan watches the pocket come away from the dress. It takes much longer to remove than he expects.

“Will you get less money?”

“I put the pocket in the wrong place. I will move it for free.”

He wants to say something kind. Instead he says, “Your pocket was straight.”

Mum looks up. A little laugh comes out of her.

“Yes. It was very straight on the wrong side.”

Ronan laughs too. Then she gives him two small scraps of cloth.

“Put one on each side of yourself.”

He does.

“Now turn towards me.”

He turns.

She points. “My right is your left. I made a mistake in my drawing.”

They make a new drawing. This one has a little face at the top. Mum writes WEARER beside it. Below the face, she draws a hand. The hand rests on the right place.

Ronan adds a large arrow.

“Do you want this?” he asks.

“I do.”

At supper, Mum has not finished. Dad takes the bowls out of her way. Ronan brings her food to the smaller stool.

“The dress can wait while you eat,” Dad says.

“The owner cannot wait until next week.”

“Eat first,” Dad says. “She asked for a pocket, not a hungry dressmaker.”

Mum puts down the needle. She eats with them. Afterwards she looks at the new drawing. Then she moves the pocket. Early the next morning, the woman comes back. She tries the dress over her other clothes. This time her free hand finds the pocket at once. She puts a key inside, takes it out and puts it back.

“That is the place,” she says.

Mum nods. Ronan stays beside the kitchen door. The woman used her free hand to reach the pocket. Ronan saw her do it. Now he understands her choice. He leaves the pocket choice to her.

Ronan puts his own hands in his trousers pockets. There is one on each side. He gives Mum a little smile.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- wearer＝穿衣服的人
- for free＝不收费
- remove＝拆除
- the wrong side＝错误的一边

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：dressmaker＝做衣服的人；scrap＝小块布。

## 读句提示

**Then she moves the pocket.**

然后／她／移动口袋。先看新图，再改口袋。

## 理解问题

1. Mum怎样弄错了口袋位置？
2. 她怎样承担并修正自己的错误？
